Dried apricots are a different product concept sold on the dried-fruit aisle in 6-8 oz bags, a different price class per pound and a different gram weight per cup, and fresh-to-dried is a standing form-flip rejection in this estate. If the existing 'apricots' id is in fact captured from dried-fruit bags, alias this term onto it instead of minting.

registrar_rulings.reason: The existing 'apricots' row is provably FRESH produce, not dried-fruit bags: I read its rule block in commodities.json (line 55665) and it explicitly EXCLUDES '\bdried\b' and 'turkish', and its live crown is Baker's PLU 4218 (url /p/apricots/0000000004218), the produce PLU for fresh apricots at $3.49/lb sold by the pound - so aliasing this term onto 'apricots' would price a recipe's dried fruit against fresh produce at roughly a quarter of the dried price class. No other id in any of the three namespaces or the feed carries dried apricots (dried-cranberries and prunes are the nearest dried-fruit rows and are different foods; 'dried-apricots' has no feed cell today, so this is 'does not exist', not merely 'unpriced'). Same food, different form = different purchase, the estate's standing fresh-vs-dried split. FOLLOW-UPS the caller must make together, not later: (1) mint 'dried-apricots' as recipe-only (recipe-board-everyday baseline + recipe-commodities.json for sale overlay) unless Brad wants it as a weekly staple; include patterns 'dried\s+apricots?' and 'apricots?,?\s+dried' and 'turkish\s+apricots?' - 'turkish' names the dried form on real labels, which is exactly why the fresh row excludes it; excludes at neighboring rigor (start from dried-cranberries' list: no yogurt-covered? judgement call, but exclude baby-food pouches, trail mix, jam/preserves, nectar, canned-in-syrup halves, granola bars); (2) add the pair apricots <-> dried-apricots to commodity-dupe-allowlist.json with reason 'fresh produce vs dried-fruit-aisle form flip' BECAUSE the audit's prefix/suffix rule WILL flag this pair - the id must arrive with its allowlist entry or the daily pages Brad on a pair already adjudicated here; (3) separately, the vocabulary needs a NEW ingredients.json row for the name 'dried apricots' (the pre-resolve found no core-word row) with macros fdc:173941 (Apricots, dried, sulfured, uncooked - the correct uncooked-dried row; 173943 is stewed-with-sugar, wrong food); the name row and the id are two acts and this ruling authorizes the id only. One watch item for capture QA, not a blocker: the fresh row's Hy-Vee cell reads $13.32/lb, ~4x the crown - worth an eyeball that a dried or specialty product hasn't leaked past the excludes there.
